Great Molasses Flood: United States. The event entered local folklore and residents reported for decades afterwards that the area still smelled of molasses on hot summer days.

The Spanish maravedí is the official currency of Kingdom of Castile. The Kingdom of Castile was a polity in the Iberian Peninsula during the Middle Ages.

Akhilesh Yadav (born 1 July 1973) is an Indian politician and national president of the Samajwadi Party, who served as the 20th Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh from 2012 to 2017.

An Lushan rebellion was a civil war in China that lasted from 755 to 763, at the approximate midpoint of the Tang dynasty (618-907).
A Franco-German joint venture dedicated to culture, this public channel carries two audio tracks so it can serve viewers in both countries at once — what's it called?
Arte (Association relative la tlvision europenne, "Association relating to European television") is a European public service channel dedicated to culture.

In 1757, the British East India Company under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal, an outcome enabled by betrayal and earlier troop commitments to Afghan invaders. What was this decisive battle?
Battle of Plassey was a decisive victory of the British East India Company, under the leadership of Robert Clive, over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies on 23 June 1757.
According to the Book of Genesis, Abraham was commanded to perform this covenant rite on a baby boy's eighth day of life, traditionally carried out by a mohel — what is it called?
Brit milah ("covenant of circumcision"), or bris, is the ceremony of circumcision in Judaism and Samaritanism during which a newborn male's foreskin is surgically removed.
Said to hail from Lycia in Asia Minor, this fire-breathing Greek monster is typically depicted as a lion with a goat's head sprouting from its back and a snake for a tail — what is it?
Chimera (mythology) (ky-MEER-ə, kih-, -MAIR-ə; lit. 'she-goat') was a monstrous fire-breathing hybrid creature in Greek mythology.
Commissioned by a judge's Transylvania Company in 1775, this frontiersman blazed the Wilderness Road through the Cumberland Gap and founded Boonesborough — which early American folk hero?
Daniel Boone was American pioneer and frontiersman (1734–1820).
Raised in Hastinapura to become crown prince, this scheming cousin of the Pandavas relied on allies like Shakuni and Karna to plot against them — who is he?
Duryodhana is the primary antagonist of the Hindu epic Mahabharata.

The stepson of Napoleon Bonaparte through his mother Joséphine's second marriage, this French statesman and military officer served in the Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars and was later adopted by the emperor — who was he?
Eugène de Beauharnais (3 September 1781 - 21 February 1824) was a French statesman and military officer who served in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
Representing Hiroshima's 1st district since 1996, this politician was foreign minister before becoming Japan's prime minister and LDP president in 2021 — who is he?
Fumio Kishida (born 29 July 1957) is a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan and President of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) from 2021 until his resignation in 2024.
Born when a papal bull elevated Cosimo I de' Medici in 1569, this Central Italian monarchy replaced a republic and was ruled by the Medici until their senior branch died out in 1737. What was it?
Grand Duchy of Tuscany was an Italian monarchy located in Central Italy that existed, with interruptions, from 1569 to 1860, replacing the Republic of Florence.

This period of Japanese history corresponds to the reign of Emperor Akihito, beginning the day after the death of his father—posthumously renamed Emperor Shōwa—in January 1989, and ending with Akihito's 2019 abdication. What is this period called?
Heisei era was the period of Japanese history corresponding to the reign of Emperor Akihito from 8 January 1989 until his abdication on 30 April 2019.
Though scholars generally consider her fictional, which legendary Chinese folk heroine is said to have lived during the Northern and Southern dynasties era?
Hua Mulan (traditional; simplified; pinyin: Hu Mln) is a legendary Chinese folk heroine from the Northern and Southern dynasties era (4th to 6th century AD) of Chinese history.
A Manhattan-raised businesswoman and Georgetown-then-Penn graduate, she became a presidential advisor from 2017 to 2021 in her father's White House — who is she?
Ivanka Trump (iv-; born October 30, 1981) is an American businesswoman.
According to the New Testament, this figure is held to be the Son of God whose crucifixion and resurrection are believed to offer humanity salvation and eternal life — who is he?
Jesus in Christianity is the Son of God as chronicled in the Bible's New Testament, and is held to be God the Son, a prosopon (person) of the Trinity of God.
A nephew of Constantine the Great, this Roman emperor rejected Christianity in favor of Neoplatonic paganism, earning him the enduring nickname 'the Apostate' — who was he?
Julian (emperor) (Ancient; 331 - 26 June 363) was the Caesar of the West from 355 to 360 and Roman emperor from 361 to 363, as well as a notable philosopher and author in Greek.
Existing from the mid-12th century to the early 20th, this western Iberian monarchy briefly anchored a transatlantic union with Brazil and the Algarves from 1815 to 1822 — which kingdom?
Kingdom of Portugal was a monarchy in the western Iberian Peninsula and the predecessor of the modern Portuguese Republic.

This Qin dynasty general served under the future First Emperor of China during the conquest of the six rival Warring States kingdoms, and was the great-great-grandfather of a famous Han dynasty general — who is he?
Li Xin (Qin) was an important Chinese military general of Qin during the Warring States era.
This Panamanian military officer ruled his country through puppet presidents in the 1980s, amassing a fortune from drug trafficking despite long ties to American intelligence — who was he?
Manuel Noriega (mahn-WEL; February 11, 1934 - May 29, 2017) was a Panamanian military officer and politician who was the de facto ruler of Panama from 1983 to 1989.

A former physician, this Azerbaijani politician serves as both First Lady and First Vice President of her country — a position her husband, the president, created in 2017 specifically to appoint her to it. Who is she?
Mehriban Aliyeva (ne Pashayeva; born 26 August 1964) is an Azerbaijani politician and former physician who is the First Vice President and First Lady of Azerbaijan.

He earned a law degree from King Saud University and advised his father before being named defence minister in 2015, then crown prince in 2017 — which grandson of Ibn Saud is now the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia?
Mohammed bin Salman (born 31 August 1985), also known as MbS, is the de facto ruler of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, formally serving as Crown Prince and Prime Minister.
Founded in 2020 by a cosmetics-company magnate, this liberal-leaning party takes a moderately supportive stance toward Vladimir Putin while opposing much of the ruling party's agenda — which party?
New People (Russia) is a political party in Russia formed in 2020.

Fought across a 630-kilometre front, this decisive offensive by the Croatian Army recaptured territory held by the self-declared Republic of Serbian Krajina in the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence — which offensive?
Operation Storm (Serbo-) was the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence and a major factor in the outcome of the Bosnian War.
An aristocrat's son and Saint-Cyr graduate, this Free-French World War II general is known in France simply by one name, and was made a Marshal of France posthumously in 1952 — who is he?
Philippe Leclerc de Hauteclocque (22 November 1902 - 28 November 1947) was a Free-French general during World War II.
This consumer-advocate lawyer wrote the 1965 book 'Unsafe at Any Speed,' which helped spur the National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act — who is he?
Ralph Nader (born February 27, 1934) is an American lawyer and political activist involved in consumer protection, environmentalism, and government reform causes.

Born into the Romney family, this Republican strategist chaired the Michigan GOP before leading the Republican National Committee from 2017 until her 2024 resignation, a tenure marked by significant electoral losses — who is she?
Ronna McDaniel (ne Romney; born March 20, 1973) is an American political strategist who served as chair of the Republican National Committee (RNC) from 2017 until her resignation in 2024.
What term, coined by 19th-century Egyptologists, describes a mysterious seafaring confederation blamed for attacks on Egypt and the Eastern Mediterranean around 1200 BC?

Sea Peoples is a phrase used to describe an unidentified seafaring confederation or group of tribes hypothesized to have attacked Egypt and other Eastern Mediterranean regions around 1200 BC during the Late Bronze Age.

Founded in the early 1900s by English occultist Aleister Crowley, this esoteric spiritual philosophy centers on discovering and following one's 'True Will,' outlined in a text he said was dictated by a non-corporeal entity — name the movement?
Thelema is a Western esoteric and occult social and spiritual philosophy, and a new religious movement.
This militant leader spent more than 25 years directing an armed campaign against the Sri Lankan government in pursuit of Tamil independence — who is he?

Velupillai Prabhakaran (26 November 1954 - 18 May 2009) was an Eelam Tamil revolutionary, guerrilla leader and a major figure of Tamil nationalism, being the founder and leader of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Aboard Apollo 8 with Borman and Lovell, this astronaut circled the Moon ten times and snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph in December 1968 — who was he?
William Anders (17 October 1933 - 7 June 2024) was a United States Air Force major general, electrical engineer, nuclear engineer, NASA astronaut, and businessman.

Alliance 90/The Greens: Green political party in Germany.

Ashoka: Mauryan emperor from 269 to 232 BCE.
This Indian engineer-turned-politician served as Karnataka's 17th chief minister from 2021 to 2023 before becoming a Lok Sabha MP for Haveri — who is he?
Basavaraj Bommai: 23rd Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2021 to 2023. In July 2022, Bommai became only the second person from BJP to complete one year as chief minister of the state.

Buckingham Palace: Official London residence of the British monarch. Buckingham Palace (UK:) is the official residence and the administrative headquarters of the monarch of the United Kingdom in London.
Derived from the Latin word for 'to assess,' this systematic count of a population's members is recommended by the UN to be conducted at least once every ten years. What is it?
Census: Compilation of information about a given population.

Growing up on the coast of Liguria, this explorer traveled as far north as the British Isles and as far south as present-day Ghana before commanding four Spanish transatlantic voyages—opening the door to European colonization of the Americas. Who was he?
Christopher Columbus: Italian navigator and explorer (1451–1506)

Crimean War: Tenth conflict of the Russo-Turkish wars (1853–1856)
The only female judge named in the Hebrew Bible, this prophetess ordered the general Barak to attack the forces of a Canaanite king — who is she?
Deborah: Prophetess in the Bible. Alternatively, "lappid" translates as "torch" or "lightning", therefore the phrase, "woman of Lappidoth" could be referencing Deborah as a "fiery woman".

Draupadi: Heroine of the ancient Hindu epic Mahabharata.

Born into a poor peasant family near Moscow and conscripted into the Imperial Russian Army, he rose to Marshal of the Soviet Union and served as Stalin's deputy commander-in-chief in World War II — who is he?

Gudrun Burwitz: Daughter of Heinrich Himmler (1929–2018)
Nicknamed "Supermac" for his wit and unflappability, this British Conservative led the country from 1957 to 1963 despite war wounds that pained him for life — who was he?
Harold Macmillan: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1957 to 1963.
Born to minor Spanish nobility, this conquistador chased riches through Hispaniola and Cuba before leading the expedition that toppled the Aztec Empire. Who was he?

Leading Bavaria's Free Voters party since 2018, this politician also serves as the state's deputy minister president and economics minister — who is he?

Inukai Tsuyoshi: Prime Minister of Japan from 1931 to 1932. Inukai Tsuyoshi (Japanese: 犬養 毅, 4 June 1855 – 15 May 1932) was a Japanese statesman who served as prime minister of Japan from 1931 to his assassination in 1932.
This 16th-century French explorer from Brittany was the first European to map the Gulf of Saint Lawrence, and borrowed an Iroquoian word for a settlement to name an entire country — who is he?
Jacques Cartier: French maritime explorer of North America (1491–1557)
Sparked by a deadly 1947 police crackdown on independence-day protesters, this guerrilla insurgency raged on a South Korean island from 1948 to 1949 — what is this event called?

Jeju uprising: 1948–1949 insurgency in South Korea. The Jeju uprising (in South Korea, the Jeju April 3 incident, Korean: 제주 4·3 사건) was an uprising on Jeju Island, South Korea, from April 1948 to May 1949.
Better known by his nickname 'Calico Jack,' this English pirate was hanged in 1720 and is remembered for his two female crew members, Anne Bonny and Mary Read — who was he?
John Rackham: English pirate (died 1720). John Rackham (hanged 18 November 1720) was an English pirate operating in the Bahamas and Jamaica during the early 18th century.
Serving as Japan's prime minister from 2001 to 2006, he ranks as the sixth-longest-serving head of government in his country's history and once held the health and welfare portfolio twice. Who is he?
Junichiro Koizumi: Prime Minister of Japan from 2001 to 2006. Coming from the prominent Koizumi family, Koizumi was first elected to the House of Representatives in 1972.
Chairman of a militant group's political bureau from 1996 to 2017, this Palestinian leader has twice served as its acting head since 2024 — who is he?

Founded in 1978 and waging an insurgency from strongholds in southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, and Syria, this militant group shifted its 1990s goal from full independence to autonomy for its people within Turkey — which organization is it?
Kurdistan Workers' Party: Kurdish militant political organization.

A former aide to Herbert Hoover turned investment banker, he became an original member and later chairman of the U.S. Atomic Energy Commission and a major figure in postwar nuclear policy — who was he?

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva: President of Brazil (2003–2011; since 2023)
A sepoy in the Bengal Native Infantry who died in April 1857, this soldier's actions helped spark the rebellion that ended East India Company rule and ushered in the British Raj — who is he?
Mangal Pandey: Indian soldier and freedom fighter (1827–1857)

Mexican Revolution: Nationwide armed struggle in Mexico (1910–1920)
Known popularly as 'General,' this Somali military officer, diplomat, and warlord lived from 1934 to 1996 — who was he?
Mohamed Farrah Aidid: Somali military officer, warlord, and disputed President of Somalia (1934–1996)

Muḥammad ibn 'Abdallāh Hassan: Somali Jihadist and anti-colonialist leader (1856–1920)

According to the Hebrew Bible, this son of Solomon and grandson of David lost the ten northern tribes to a rebellion around 932 BCE, becoming the first king of the southern Kingdom of Judah — who is he?
Rehoboam: Biblical figure; first monarch of the Kingdom of Judah.
A human-rights lawyer who rode a wave of younger internet users into office, this man served as South Korea's ninth president from 2003 to 2008 — who is he?
Roh Moo-hyun: President of South Korea from 2003 to 2008. Roh's pre-presidential political career was focused on human rights advocacy for student activists in South Korea.

The only person ever elected governor of two different US states, he also served as president of the Republic of Texas after spending years living with the Cherokee, who nicknamed him 'Raven' — who was he?
Sam Houston: American general and statesman (1793–1863)
Co-leading a pro-Kurdish party to double-digit vote shares in Turkey's 2015 elections, this politician ran for president from behind bars in 2018 after his 2016 imprisonment — who is he?
Selahattin Demirtaş: Turkish politician. Selahattin Demirtaş (born 10 April 1973) is a Kurdish politician, lawyer and author.

This second emperor of Vietnam's Trần dynasty handed the throne to his son yet stayed on as 'retired emperor,' co-commanding the victories that repelled two Mongol invasions of Đại Việt — who was he?
Trần Thánh Tông: Emperor of Đại Việt from 1258 to 1278.

Victor Emmanuel III: King of Italy from 1900 to 1946.

War in Donbas: 2014–2022 war between Ukraine and Russia.

Winfield Scott: United States Army general (1786–1866)

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
John Archibald Wheeler is a physicist. John Archibald Wheeler (July 9, 1911 – April 13, 2008) was an American theoretical physicist.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Émilie du Châtelet is a mathematician. It circulated widely, generated heated debates, and was translated into German and Italian in 1743.
What is the atomic number of Darmstadtium?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
What is the atomic number of Gold?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
In what year did Kitty Oppenheimer die?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was Boron discovered?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
Dopamine: Pfizer. Dopamine (DA, a contraction of 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine) is a neuromodulatory molecule that plays several important roles in cells.
In which country is TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkey. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Who is credited with discovering Apus?
Apus: Petrus Plancius. Apus is a small constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Cat's Eye Nebula?
Cat's Eye Nebula: William Herschel. It is a well-studied object that has been observed from radio to X-ray wavelengths.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen?
Hydrogen: Henry Cavendish. Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Who is credited with discovering Astatine?
Astatine: Emilio G. Segrè. Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.

Born into a prominent Stockholm family, this fluent-in-six-languages inventor filed his first patent at 24 and went on to hold 355 in all, while owning the arms-and-engineering firm Bofors. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel (noh-BEL; 21 October 1833 - 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.

Native to tropical America and carried across the Pacific by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this small tree in the same family as soursop produces a scaly-skinned fruit with sweet, creamy flesh — what's the species?
Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
This genus of roughly 300 evergreen flowering plants includes one edible species enjoyed as a vegetable and another grown purely as an ornamental — which genus?
Asparagus (genus) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Asparagoideae.

Found naturally in many plants and abbreviated "Bz," this white crystalline compound is the simplest of the aromatic carboxylic acids and lends its salts to the world of food preservatives — what is it?
Benzoic acid is a white or colorless crystalline organic compound with the formula C6H5COOH, whose structure consists of a benzene ring (C6H6) with a carboxyl (C(=O)OH) substituent.
Every subatomic particle is either this integer-spin class or a fermion; Paul Dirac named the class after physicist Satyendra Nath Bose, whose statistics they obey — what's the class called?
Boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
With the chemical formula CaO, this white, caustic, alkaline solid is produced by heating limestone and has been used since antiquity in construction and agriculture — what's the compound's name?
Calcium oxide (formula: CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.
Their name is Greek for "head-feet," and fishers sometimes call them "inkfish" for their ink-squirting trick; squid, octopus and nautilus all belong. What's this molluscan class?
Cephalopod is any member of the molluscan class Cephalopoda (Greek plural, kephalpodes; "head-feet") such as a squid, octopus, cuttlefish, or nautilus.
After serving as dean of Harvard's Faculty of Arts and Sciences, this political scientist became the university's 30th president in July 2023 — who is she?
Claudine Gay (born August 4, 1970) is an American political scientist who is the Wilbur A. Cowett Professor of Government and of African and African-American Studies at Harvard University.
This group of related RNA viruses causes respiratory illnesses ranging from the mild common cold to deadly diseases like SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 — what's this virus family called?
Coronavirus are a group of related RNA viruses that cause diseases in mammals and birds.
Known mostly through DNA evidence rather than abundant fossils, this extinct group of archaic humans ranged across Asia between roughly 200,000 and 32,000 years ago — what are they called?
Denisovan (d-(nz)) are an extinct species or subspecies of archaic human that ranged across Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene, approximately 200,000-32,000 years ago.

This hypothetical megastructure would encircle an entire star to capture most of its energy output, conceived as a thought experiment for how an advanced civilization might meet growing power needs — what's the concept called?
Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

This genus's tapering spacing of stem nodes toward the tip is credited with inspiring John Napier's work on logarithms; today it's the sole living genus of an ancient, spore-producing plant lineage nicknamed horsetail — which genus?
Equisetum (horsetail) is the only living genus in Equisetaceae, a family of vascular plants that reproduce by spores rather than seeds.
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.

This Austrian engineer founded a firearms company in 1963; when his first pistol entered Austrian service in 1982, its famous model number referred to his 17th patent, not the rounds it held — who is he?
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland
Gaston Glock (19 July 1929 - 27 December 2023) was an Austrian engineer and businessman.
What common name covers a diverse family of marine ray-finned fish in the order Perciformes, most belonging to the genera Epinephelus or Mycteroperca?
Grouper are a diverse group of marine ray-finned fish in the family Epinephelidae, in the order Perciformes.
Named after the physicist who first proved the existence of electromagnetic waves, this SI unit measures one cycle per second. What unit is it?
Hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.

Ranging from mild headaches and poor balance to severe confusion and seizures, this low-blood-sodium condition can be triggered by causes as varied as vomiting, diuretics, or overhydration — what's it called?
Hyponatremia is a low concentration of sodium in the blood. It is generally defined as a sodium concentration of less than 135 mmol/L (135 mEq/L), with severe hyponatremia being below 120 mEq/L.
Serving as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician played a central role in creating the European single market and laying groundwork for the euro — who is he?
Jacques Delors (20 July 1925 - 27 December 2023) was a French politician who served as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995.

An evergreen conifer in the cypress family, this small tree or shrub boasts the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere — which species?
Juniperus communis is a species of small tree or shrub in the cypress family Cupressaceae.

Amphoteric and unreactive, this post-transition metal reacts with both acids and bases, melts at a low temperature, and tarnishes from shiny to dull gray in air — and three of its isotopes end major nuclear decay chains. Which element is it?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.
Based on a commercial airliner design, this four-engine turboprop aircraft hunts submarines for the U.S. Navy using a distinctive tail-mounted magnetic detector — what plane is it?
Lockheed P-3 Orion is a four-engined, turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed for the United States Navy and introduced in the 1960s.

With over 2,400 species sporting triangular heads, bulging eyes on flexible necks, and folded forelegs built to snatch prey, these insects count termites and cockroaches among their closest relatives — what are they?
Mantis are an order (Mantodea) of insects that contains over 2,400 species in about 460 genera in 33 families.
This medication treats nausea, vomiting, and acid reflux by blocking dopamine receptors, but is rarely recommended for more than twelve weeks due to a risk of movement disorders — what drug is it?
Metoclopramide is a medication used to treat nausea, vomiting, gastroparesis, and gastroesophageal reflux disease.
This small green legume, cultivated widely across East and South Asia, is used in both savory dishes and sweet desserts — what is it?
Mung bean (Vigna radiata) is a plant species in the legume family.

Found across 26 African countries in lakes, rivers and swamps — with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana — adult males of this reptile can stretch past five meters; what is it?
Nile crocodile (Crocodylus niloticus) is a large crocodilian native to freshwater habitats in Africa, where it is present in 26 countries.
Named from the Greek word for 'smell,' this hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and is often alloyed for fountain pen nib tips — which element?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek (osm) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
Commercially produced from citrus fruits as a white-to-light-brown powder, this plant-cell-wall polysaccharide is the gelling agent that makes jams and jellies set — what is it?
Pectin (Ancient) is a heteropolysaccharide, a structural polymer contained in the cell walls and middle lamellae of terrestrial plants.
Confirming and popularizing Isaac Newton's work, this French scholar authored the five-volume 'Mécanique céleste' and helped pioneer the Bayesian view of probability — who is he?

Pierre-Simon Laplace (23 March 1749 - 5 March 1827) was a French polymath, a scholar whose work has been instrumental in the fields of physics, astronomy, mathematics, engineering, statistics, and philosophy.
Legally defined as exactly 0.45359237 kilograms and divided into 16 avoirdupois ounces, this unit of mass is used in both British imperial and U.S. customary systems — what is it?
Pound (mass) is a unit of mass used in both the British imperial and United States customary systems of measurement.
Used to treat malaria and babesiosis, this medication also gives tonic water its distinctive bitter taste — what is it?
Quinine is a medication used to treat malaria and babesiosis. While sometimes used for nocturnal leg cramps, quinine is not recommended for this purpose due to the risk of serious side effects.
A Jesuit priest, poet, and diplomat from the Republic of Ragusa, this polymath produced an early precursor of atomic theory and in 1753 discovered the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich (18 May 1711 - 13 February 1787) was a physicist, astronomer, mathematician, philosopher, diplomat, poet, theologian, Jesuit priest, and a polymath from the Republic of Ragusa.

After early attempts at family-friendly Christian video games found little success, this American developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise about animatronic mascots that come alive at night — who is he?

Scott Cawthon (born June 4, 1978) is an American video game developer, writer, and producer best known for creating Five Nights at Freddy's, a series of horror video games which expanded into a media franchise.
Famous for their slowness, these tree-dwelling Neotropical mammals are closest relatives of anteaters and come in just seven living species across two genera — what are they?
Sloth are a Neotropical group of xenarthran mammals constituting the suborder Folivora, including the extant arboreal tree sloths and extinct terrestrial ground sloths.
Innervated by the accessory nerve, which of the body's largest and most superficial neck structures rotates the head to the opposite side and flexes the neck?
Sternocleidomastoid muscle is one of the largest and most superficial cervical muscles.

Known for a leather-like smell when freshly milled and prized for durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood tree bears small, fragrant white flowers and large, papery, often-hairy leaves — name this tree?
Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood tree species in the family Lamiaceae.
This muscular organ in the mouth manipulates food for chewing and swallowing, serves as the body's primary organ of taste, and also enables human speech — what organ is it?
Tongue is a muscular organ in the mouth of a typical tetrapod.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial flowering plant is the type species of its genus and a member of the honeysuckle family — which herb?
Valerian (herb) (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
This Austrian physicist earned a 1945 Nobel Prize for the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the existence of what would become known as the neutrino — who is he?
Wolfgang Pauli (25 April 1900 - 15 December 1958) was an Austrian theoretical physicist and a pioneer of quantum mechanics.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
A striking red-capped, white-warted mushroom of northern forests, this fungus may owe its name to an old use against flies — or to a medieval belief that flies caused madness. What is it?
Amanita muscaria: Species of mushroom. Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete fungus of the genus Amanita.
Native to the eastern Mediterranean, this flowering herb's seeds taste similar to fennel, licorice, and tarragon and flavor candies and spirits — what is it?
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.

This infraorder of decapod crustaceans tucks a stubby tail-like abdomen under a hard shell and ends its front pair of legs in pincers — over 1.5 million tonnes of them are eaten by humans yearly. What group is it?
Brachyura: Crustacean. The true crabs are the largest of the crab decapod groups with carcinised body forms.
Common in cancer, heart failure, and other serious illnesses, this syndrome causes muscle wasting that better nutrition alone can't reverse — what is it?
In 1886 this German engineer patented what's considered the first practical automobile, and his Mannheim company later merged with Daimler — who is he?
Carl Benz: German designer and engineer (1844–1929)
Documented anatomically since the time of Hippocrates over 2,000 years ago, this roughly 4-centimeter-long fibromuscular organ connects the vagina to the uterine cavity. What structure is this?
Cervix: Lower part of the uterus in the female reproductive system.
This Dutch scientist discovered Saturn's largest moon and invented the pendulum clock, the most accurate timekeeper for nearly three centuries — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens: Dutch mathematician and physicist (1629–1695)
Thought extinct since the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this lobe-finned fish was found alive off the west Indian Ocean, more closely related to lungfish than typical fish — what is it?
A heart disease involving reduced blood flow to cardiac muscle due to buildup of plaque in heart arteries — the most common cardiovascular disease. What is it?
Coronary artery disease: Reduction of blood flow to the heart. Procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG) may be used in severe disease.
Named after the bladder because it was first found in urine, this amino acid carries a thiol group that lets it forge the disulfide bonds holding many proteins together. Which amino acid is it?
Cysteine: Proteinogenic amino acid. Cysteine (symbol Cys or C) is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid with the formula HS−CH2−CH(NH2)−COOH.

Doctors once spotted this endocrine condition by its three Ps — polydipsia, polyuria, and polyphagia, or excessive thirst, urination, and hunger — all tracing back to trouble with insulin. Which disease is it?
Diabetes: Group of endocrine diseases characterized by high blood sugar levels.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
Native to southern India, this ginger-family plant produces the aromatic seeds used in both sweet and savory cooking — what is it, botanically?
Elettaria cardamomum: Species of flowering plant.
This fibromuscular tube carries food from throat to stomach using peristaltic contractions, and its name traces to Ancient Greek roots meaning roughly 'I carry what I ate.' What is it?
Esophagus: Vertebrate organ through which food passes to the stomach.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'to lead out,' this scholarly practice of critically interpreting a text — often the Bible — also examines its historical background and literary genre — what is it called?
Exegesis: Critical investigation of a text.
From the Latin word for 'tube' or 'pipe,' this medical term describes an abnormal connection between two hollow spaces in the body — what is it?
Fistula: Abnormal connection between two hollow bodily spaces, often organs.
Sold under the brand name Lasix, this loop diuretic treats edema from heart failure and kidney disease and can also cause tinnitus and light sensitivity?

Furosemide: Loop diuretic medication. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
Caught from contaminated water and common among travelers and children, this parasitic infection causes fatty, sticky diarrhea weeks after exposure — what is it?
Giardiasis: Parasitic disease that results in diarrhea.
Sporting pied black-and-white plumage with a red patch on its lower belly, this Palearctic bird drums on trees to mark territory and excavate nest holes — which species?
Great spotted woodpecker: Species of bird. The great spotted woodpecker (Dendrocopos major) is a medium-sized woodpecker with pied black and white plumage and a red patch on the lower belly.
A young one of this fast-running lagomorph is called a leveret, and a group of them may be known as a 'husk' or a 'down'?
Hare: Genus of mammals in the family Leporidae.
Known scientifically as singultus, this involuntary diaphragm spasm closes the glottis in about 35 milliseconds to produce a signature sound — what reflex is it?
Hiccup: Involuntary contraction of the diaphragm. The rhythm of the hiccup, or the time between hiccups, tends to be relatively constant.

Made of one oxygen and one hydrogen atom bonded together with a negative charge, this ion is the active base in the sodium compound used to produce millions of tons of industrial chemicals yearly. What ion is it?

According to psychologist Alfred Adler, this persistent feeling of being deficient or lesser than others — often stemming from childhood comparisons to a sibling — can lead people to overcompensate. What is it called?
Inferiority complex: Intense feeling of inadequacy and inferior.
This neo-Keynesian economist gave his name to a model for censored data — the 'tobit' — while advising the Fed and championing government action against recessions; who is he?
James Tobin: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2002)
This French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and a crater on the Moon is named after him; who was he?
Living as a recluse in a log house outside Kaluga, this Russian pioneer of rocket science inspired both Wernher von Braun and the architects of the Soviet space program — who is he?
Also called Hansen's disease, this slow bacterial infection dulls the body's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed injuries can cost a person their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy: Chronic disease caused by bacterial infection.
Normally solitary and harmless, these short-horned grasshoppers can undergo a serotonin-triggered shift into gregarious swarming behavior under drought-then-growth conditions — what are they called?
Locust: Grasshopper that has a swarming phase.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).

Born from a US-UK cooperative effort begun in the early 1970s to improve on a first-generation jump jet, this vertical-takeoff-capable attack aircraft has served the US Marine Corps plus Spanish and Italian navies — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II: Anglo-American VSTOL ground-attack aircraft.
Sold under the brand name Medrol, this synthetic steroid can trigger iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome if not carefully tapered after high-dose use for acute flares — name the drug?
Its dust-like, colored, fuzzy appearance on food comes from spores, and its branching network of hyphae — called a mycelium — counts as a single organism; what fungal structure is this?
Mold: Wooly, dust-like fungal structure or substance.
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
This British-American historian, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution, writes on financial history and holds notably favorable views of the British Empire — who is he?
Known as holy basil and sacred within the Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism, which aromatic herb is widely used in Ayurvedic tea?
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Species of flowering plant.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
Named Pisum sativum by Carl Linnaeus in 1753, this pulse crop's pods are botanically a fruit containing seeds with green or yellow cotyledons — what vegetable is it?
Pea: Species of plant with edible seeds.

Combining textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly field traces its classical roots to the libraries of Pergamum and Alexandria in the 4th century BC — what is it?
Philology: Study of language in historical sources.
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Once one of America's leading rocket experts with an MIT aeronautics degree, he was deported to China in 1955 and went on to father that nation's space program — which aerospace engineer?

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.
Also known as sixth disease, this childhood viral infection typically strikes before age three with a sudden fever followed by a pink rash lasting under three days — what's the condition called?
Roseola: Human disease caused by human herpesviruses.

Sometimes nicknamed the "seven-year itch," this contagious infestation by a tiny burrowing mite spreads fastest in crowded places and announces itself with fierce itching and a pimple-like rash — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
Famous for kite-shaped plates along its back and spikes on its tail, this Late Jurassic herbivore may have been preyed on by Allosaurus — which dinosaur?
Stegosaurus: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur.
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
The primary male sex hormone, this androgen builds muscle and bone, spurs body hair, and is even linked to mood, courtship display and dominance in both sexes — what is it?
Testosterone: Primary male sex hormone. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
One of only a few fish able to keep its body warmer than the surrounding water, this fast-swimming ocean predator's yellowfin members can reach 75 km/h — what is it?
Tuna: Tribe of fish. Tuna (pl.: tunas or tuna) is a saltwater fish that belongs to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the Scombridae (mackerel) family.
Caused by white blood cells migrating into and damaging vessel walls, this group of disorders inflames both arteries and veins, and sometimes even the lymphatic vessels — what condition is it?
Vasculitis: Medical disorders that destroy blood vessels by inflammation.
Nicknamed the 'cock-of-the-woods,' this ground-dwelling grouse is the largest of all its kind, with males growing to nearly twice the size of females — which bird?
Western capercaillie: Species of bird. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Xenon is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for xenon is Xe. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Bismuth is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for bismuth is Bi. Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
